ambiguities.text: The specification does not define error handling if rpc.discover is called but the service cannot generate the OpenRPC document.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume standard JSON-RPC error response should be returned with appropriate error code if document generation fails.

ambiguities.text: It is unclear whether the OpenRPC document should reflect runtime-available methods or all theoretically supported methods.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the document should reflect currently available methods based on node configuration and capabilities.

ambiguities.text: The specification mentions 'different method signatures across clients' but does not specify how to handle method signature conflicts.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume each client returns its own method signatures; consumers must handle client-specific differences.

implicit_assumptions.description: The OpenRPC document returned by rpc.discover is assumed to be accurate and not tampered with.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: A malicious node could return incorrect method specifications, leading to client-side validation bypasses or unexpected behavior.

implicit_assumptions.description: The JSON-RPC connection is assumed to be secure (e.g., over HTTPS or local IPC).
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Man-in-the-middle attacks could modify the OpenRPC document in transit, causing clients to use incorrect API specifications.

implicit_assumptions.description: Service implementers will keep the OpenRPC document synchronized with actual method implementations.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Stale or outdated OpenRPC documents could lead to failed API calls or security vulnerabilities if deprecated methods are still listed.
